transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I came in because... I just can't stop focusing on my jaw and my neck. There's this sagging, uneven spot right there, and it's all I can see. People tell me it looks normal, but I just know it's the first thing anyone notices. When I'm at work doing hair, or talking to the nurses, or even just at church... I feel like everyone is staring right at it.

Can you tell me what you think is wrong with the sagging or uneven spot on your jaw and neck? Do you think it’s something that can still be fixed, or do you feel like it’s a permanent flaw that people must notice?

Well, like I was just saying, I just can't stop seeing it. It's this sagging, uneven area right along here. To me, it just looks wrong, like this glaring, permanent flaw. I don't know if there's a way to fix it, but right now it feels like it's just stuck there for everyone to see. 

Even when folks try to reassure me and tell me it looks completely normal, I just don't believe them. No matter what they say, I still feel like it’s the absolute first thing the families I work with, the nurses, or the people at my church notice when they look at my face.
Does this concern about your jaw and neck make it hard for you to focus on your work, interact with others, or enjoy activities you used to like?

Yeah, it really does. At work, I've actually passed up chances to help lead meetings or take on any of the supervisory pieces. I just worry that if I'm up in front of everyone, they'll just be looking right at my face and neck the whole time. And... I've even fallen behind on my paperwork lately because I get stuck for so long just trying to make myself look presentable before I can even start my day. 

It affects my free time, too. I’ve stopped going to some of my book club and walking club activities. Honestly, just the whole process of getting ready and trying to hide it... it just feels like too much right now.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching your jaw or neck, or trying to cover it up, because of how you feel about its appearance?

Yes, I do that a lot. Before I leave for work or... or for a meeting, I just keep going back to the bathroom mirror. I'll stand there fixing my collar, trying to position my hair around my neck to cover it up. And then, even when I think I'm ready, I'll pull out my phone camera to take another look just to be sure. 

I also catch myself asking my daughter if it looks strange before I leave. Honestly, doing all of that over and over has made me late more than once. I just can't seem to walk out the door without checking it a few times.
